stem: To compare two sets of data fully, which two things should you compare?

options.content: An average and a measure of spread
options.rationale: One tells you which set is higher; the other tells you which is more consistent.

options.content: The largest value and the smallest value
options.rationale: These give only the range of each set.

options.content: The mean and the median
options.rationale: These are both averages; you also need a measure of spread.

options.content: The number of values in each set
options.rationale: The sizes of the sets do not tell you how the values compare.

explanation: A full comparison uses an average (mean, median or mode) to say which set is generally higher, and a measure of spread (range or interquartile range) to say which set is more consistent.

stem: True or false: if one set of marks has a larger range than another, its marks are more spread out (less consistent).

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct: a larger range means a bigger gap between the highest and lowest values, so the data are less consistent.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true: the range measures spread, so a larger range means the data are more spread out.

explanation: The range is a measure of spread. A larger range shows that the values are more varied, that is, less consistent.

stem:
The table shows the maximum temperature, in $^\circ\text{C}$, recorded at a school weather station on each day of one week.

| Day | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Temperature (°C) | 24 | 27 | 29 | 31 | 28 | 22 | 25 |

Find the difference between the highest and the lowest temperature.
explanation: The highest temperature is $31^\circ\text{C}$ (Thursday) and the lowest is $22^\circ\text{C}$ (Saturday), so the difference is $31 - 22 = 9^\circ\text{C}$.
hints: Find the largest and smallest values in the table.

stem: The marks of two groups in a test are summarised: Group A has median 34 and range 12; Group B has median 29 and range 20. Which statement is correct?

options.content: Group A did better on average and its marks were more consistent.
options.rationale: A has the higher median and the smaller range.

options.content: Group B did better on average because its range is larger.
options.rationale: The range measures spread, not how well a group did.

options.content: Group A did better on average but its marks were less consistent.
options.rationale: A smaller range (12) means **more** consistent marks.

options.content: The groups did equally well because $34 - 29 = 5$ is small.
options.rationale: A difference of 5 in the medians still shows A did better on average.

explanation: On average Group A scored higher (median 34 compared with 29). Group A's marks were also more consistent, because its range (12) is smaller than Group B's (20).
hints: Use the median to compare averages and the range to compare consistency.

stem:
The table shows the items sold at a small shop in Chinhoyi on three days.

| Item | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maize meal (bags) | 14 | 18 | 11 |
| Sugar (packets) | 22 | 25 | 19 |
| Cooking oil (bottles) | 9 | 12 | 8 |

How many items were sold altogether on Tuesday?
explanation: Tuesday's column: $18 + 25 + 12 = 55$ items.

stem: A school's newsletter shows its pass rate rising from 71% in 2024 to 74% in 2025 on a bar chart. The vertical axis starts at 70%, so the 2025 bar looks four times as tall as the 2024 bar. Why is the chart misleading?

options.content: Because the vertical axis does not start at zero, a small difference looks large.
options.rationale: Starting at 70% removes most of each bar, exaggerating the difference.

options.content: Because pass rates should be shown on a pie chart.
options.rationale: A bar chart is a sensible way to compare two years; the problem is the axis.

options.content: Because 74 is not four times 71.
options.rationale: True, but the reason the chart gives that impression is the axis starting at 70%.

options.content: Because the bars are the same width.
options.rationale: Bars of equal width are correct.

explanation: With the axis starting at 70%, the bars are 1 and 4 units tall, so 2025 looks four times better. In fact the pass rate rose by only 3 percentage points. Bar charts should normally have a vertical axis starting at zero.
hints: Where does the vertical axis start?

stem: A survey of 40 shoppers at one supermarket in Bulawayo found that 26 of them prefer brand X of cooking oil. Which conclusion is justified by this survey?

options.content: 65% of the shoppers in this sample preferred brand X.
options.rationale: This describes the sample exactly, without going beyond it.

options.content: 65% of people in Zimbabwe prefer brand X.
options.rationale: The sample is small and from one supermarket, so it may not represent everyone.

options.content: Every shopper at the supermarket prefers brand X.
options.rationale: 14 of the 40 shoppers in the sample did not.

options.content: Brand X is the best cooking oil.
options.rationale: The survey measured preference, not quality, and only in one small sample.

explanation: The data describe only the 40 shoppers surveyed: $\frac{26}{40} = 65\%$ of them preferred brand X. Claims about everyone in Zimbabwe, or about which oil is best, are not supported by a small sample from one supermarket.
hints: Which statement stays within the group that was actually asked?

stem: A farmer's groundnut yield rose from $2.5$ tonnes in one season to $3.1$ tonnes in the next. Calculate the percentage increase.
explanation: Increase $= 3.1 - 2.5 = 0.6$ tonnes. Percentage increase $= \dfrac{0.6}{2.5} \times 100 = 24\%$.
hints: Divide the increase by the **original** yield.

stem:
The marks of ten learners in each of two classes are listed.

Class X: 41, 48, 52, 55, 58, 60, 63, 67, 72, 84

Class Y: 50, 53, 55, 57, 58, 60, 61, 62, 64, 70

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Find the mean mark of Class X.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Find the range of the marks of Class Y.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The mean of Class Y is 59 and the range of Class X is 43. Make **two** comparisons between the marks of the two classes.

points.description: Average: on average Class X scored (slightly) higher, mean 60 compared with 59
Spread: Class Y's marks were more consistent, range 20 compared with 43

explanation: Class X: total 600, mean $= 60$; range $= 84 - 41 = 43$. Class Y: total 590, mean $= 59$; range $= 70 - 50 = 20$. On average Class X did slightly better, but Class Y's marks were much more consistent.
workedSolution:
1. (a) $\frac{600}{10} = 60$.
2. (b) $70 - 50 = 20$.
3. (c) Average: X higher (60 v 59). Spread: Y more consistent (range 20 v 43).
hints: One comparison should use the means and the other the ranges.

stem: True or false: if the mean mark of Class A is higher than the mean mark of Class B, then every learner in Class A scored more than every learner in Class B.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: A mean summarises the whole class. Some learners in Class B can still score more than some learners in Class A.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct: a higher mean only tells you about the class on average, not about every individual.

explanation: An average describes a group as a whole. For example, marks of 40 and 90 (mean 65) and marks of 60 and 62 (mean 61): the first group has the higher mean, yet its 40 is lower than both marks in the second group.
hints: Try two small groups of marks with different means and see whether the values overlap.

stem:
The table shows Chipo's marks in five subjects in two terms.

| Subject | Mathematics | English | Shona | Geography | Biology |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Term 1 | 64 | 58 | 71 | 49 | 66 |
| Term 2 | 69 | 61 | 70 | 57 | 72 |

In which subject did her mark improve the most?

options.content: Geography
options.rationale: $57 - 49 = 8$, the largest increase.

options.content: Biology
options.rationale: $72 - 66 = 6$, less than Geography's increase.

options.content: Mathematics
Shona
options.rationale: $70 - 71 = -1$: her Shona mark went down.

explanation: The changes are Mathematics $+5$, English $+3$, Shona $-1$, Geography $+8$ and Biology $+6$. The largest improvement is in Geography. (Biology has the highest Term 2 mark, but that is not the biggest improvement.)
hints: Work out Term 2 − Term 1 for each subject.

stem:
Two schools in different districts each recorded their rainfall, in mm, for the same six months.

| Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| School P | 120 | 95 | 60 | 20 | 5 | 0 |
| School Q | 85 | 80 | 70 | 45 | 30 | 10 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Find the mean monthly rainfall at School P.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Find the mean monthly rainfall at School Q, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Find the range of the rainfall at School P.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The range at School Q is 75 mm. Compare the rainfall at the two schools.

points.description: On average School Q had (slightly) more rain per month (53.3 mm compared with 50 mm)
School P's rainfall was more variable (range 120 mm compared with 75 mm); Q's was more consistent

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Which statement about the reliability of these comparisons is most sensible?

options.content: They are based on only six months of one year, so other years could be different.
options.rationale: Six months of data is a small sample of the weather.

options.content: They prove that School Q always gets more rain than School P.
options.rationale: One set of six months cannot prove what always happens.

options.content: They are completely reliable because the rain was measured.
options.rationale: Accurate measurement does not make a small sample representative.

options.content: They show that rain falls more in January everywhere in Zimbabwe.
options.rationale: Two schools cannot represent the whole country.

explanation: School P: total 300 mm, mean 50 mm, range $120 - 0 = 120$ mm. School Q: total 320 mm, mean $53.3$ mm, range 75 mm. On average Q was slightly wetter, while P's rainfall varied much more from month to month. The data cover only six months of one year, so the conclusions are limited.
workedSolution:
1. (a) $\frac{120 + 95 + 60 + 20 + 5 + 0}{6} = \frac{300}{6} = 50$ mm.
2. (b) $\frac{320}{6} = 53.33\ldots \approx 53.3$ mm.
3. (c) $120 - 0 = 120$ mm.
4. (d) Q wetter on average; P more variable.
5. (e) Small sample (six months of one year).
hints: For School P, the smallest value is 0.

stem:
The table shows the number of days that each of 40 learners was absent last term.

| Days absent | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of learners | 12 | 9 | 7 | 5 | 4 | 3 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How many learners were absent for more than 3 days?

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What percentage of the learners were never absent?

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Find the total number of days of absence for the 40 learners.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The head teacher says, "Most learners missed at least one day." Is this correct?

options.content: Yes: 28 of the 40 learners missed at least one day.
options.rationale: $40 - 12 = 28$, which is more than half.

options.content: No: 12 learners were never absent.
options.rationale: 12 is fewer than half of 40, so most learners did miss at least one day.

options.content: No: the mode is 0 days.
options.rationale: The mode is 0, but the other values together make up most of the class.

options.content: It cannot be decided from the table.
options.rationale: The table gives enough information: $40 - 12 = 28$.

explanation: (a) $4 + 3 = 7$ learners. (b) $\frac{12}{40} \times 100 = 30\%$. (c) Multiply each number of days by its frequency and add: $0 \times 12 + 1 \times 9 + 2 \times 7 + 3 \times 5 + 4 \times 4 + 5 \times 3 = 0 + 9 + 14 + 15 + 16 + 15 = 69$ days. (d) $40 - 12 = 28$ learners missed at least one day, which is more than half, so the statement is correct.
workedSolution:
1. (a) 4 days: 4 learners; 5 days: 3 learners; total 7.
2. (b) $\frac{12}{40} \times 100 = 30\%$.
3. (c) $9 + 14 + 15 + 16 + 15 = 69$ days.
4. (d) $40 - 12 = 28 > 20$: most learners missed at least one day.
hints: For the total, multiply each number of days by its frequency and add.

stem: A study finds that learners who eat breakfast every day tend to get higher marks. A newspaper headline says: "Eating breakfast makes you cleverer." What is the best criticism of the headline?

options.content: A link between two things does not prove that one causes the other; other factors could explain both.
options.rationale: For example, family support might affect both breakfast and study habits.

options.content: The study should have used the median instead of the mean.
options.rationale: The choice of average does not affect whether one thing causes another.

options.content: Breakfast cannot be measured.
options.rationale: Whether a learner eats breakfast can easily be recorded.

options.content: Higher marks always mean lower spread.
options.rationale: Average and spread are separate ideas, and this does not address the claim.

explanation: The study shows an association (a correlation), not a cause. Other factors, such as home support, sleep or family income, could influence both eating breakfast and marks. The headline claims more than the data can show.
hints: Does "tend to go together" mean "one causes the other"?

stem:
A school tuck shop's takings, in US dollars, for six months are shown in the table.

| Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Takings (US\$) | 420 | 385 | 460 | 512 | 398 | 475 |

Calculate the mean monthly takings, correct to the nearest dollar.
workedSolution:
1. Total $= 2650$. **(M1)**
2. Mean $= \frac{2650}{6} = 441.666\ldots \approx 442$ to the nearest dollar. **(A1)** (An unrounded answer such as 441.67 earns the M1 only.)
hints: Add the six values and divide by 6.

stem:
The times, in minutes, that 11 learners in each of two groups took to complete a puzzle are shown in order.

Group 1: 12, 15, 18, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26, 28, 31, 40

Group 2: 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Find the median time for Group 1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Find the interquartile range for Group 1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Find the interquartile range for Group 2.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The median for Group 2 is 22 minutes. Compare the times of the two groups.

points.description: On average Group 2 was (slightly) quicker: median 22 minutes compared with 23 minutes
Group 2's times were more consistent: IQR 5 minutes compared with 10 minutes

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Why is the interquartile range a better measure of spread than the range for Group 1?

options.content: It is not affected by the extreme time of 40 minutes.
options.rationale: The IQR uses only the middle half of the data.

options.content: It is always larger than the range.
options.rationale: The IQR is never larger than the range.

options.content: It uses every value in the data.
options.rationale: The range and IQR both use only a few values; the IQR ignores the extremes.

options.content: It is easier to calculate.
options.rationale: The range is easier to calculate; the IQR is better because it resists extreme values.

explanation: Group 1: median = 6th value $= 23$; lower quartile = 3rd value $= 18$; upper quartile = 9th value $= 28$; IQR $= 10$. Group 2: lower quartile $= 20$, upper quartile $= 25$, IQR $= 5$. Group 2 was slightly quicker on average and much more consistent. The IQR ignores the unusually slow time of 40 minutes, which inflates the range of Group 1.
workedSolution:
1. $n = 11$: median is the 6th value, quartiles are the 3rd and 9th values.
2. Group 1: $Q_1 = 18$, median $= 23$, $Q_3 = 28$, IQR $= 28 - 18 = 10$.
3. Group 2: $Q_1 = 20$, median $= 22$, $Q_3 = 25$, IQR $= 25 - 20 = 5$.
4. Compare: Group 2 lower median (quicker) and smaller IQR (more consistent).
hints: With 11 ordered values, the quartiles are the 3rd and 9th values.
A lower time is better in a puzzle race.

stem: Match each feature of a diagram with the reason it can mislead. One reason is not used.

left.content: The vertical axis of a bar chart starts at 90
A pictogram uses symbols of different sizes
A pie chart is drawn tilted in 3-D
A line graph has no numbers on its vertical axis

right.content: Small differences look much bigger than they are
Bigger symbols look like more than the value they stand for
Sectors at the front look larger than those at the back
The values cannot be read at all
The bars are all the same width

explanation: A truncated axis exaggerates differences; unequal pictogram symbols distort the comparison because area grows faster than height; 3-D tilting makes front sectors look bigger; a missing scale means the reader cannot read values. Bars of equal width are correct and not misleading.
hints: For each feature, ask what false impression it gives.

stem: A researcher wants to find out how Form 4 learners in a district travel to school. Which sample is most likely to be representative?

options.content: 100 Form 4 learners chosen at random from all the schools in the district
options.rationale: Random selection from every school gives every Form 4 learner a chance of being chosen.

options.content: 100 Form 4 learners from the largest school in the district
options.rationale: One school may not be typical (for example, a town school with many kombi users).

options.content: The first 100 Form 4 learners to arrive at a district sports day
options.rationale: Early arrivals may mostly come by car or bus, so the sample is biased.

options.content: 10 Form 4 learners chosen at random from the district
options.rationale: Random is good, but 10 learners is too small a sample to be reliable.

explanation: A representative sample is chosen at random from the whole population and is large enough. Choosing from one school, or from the first arrivals, introduces bias; a sample of 10 is too small.
hints: Look for a sample that is both random and large, and drawn from the whole district.

stem: In 2024, 120 of the 160 candidates at a school passed Mathematics. In 2025, 135 of the 200 candidates passed. The headteacher says, "More candidates passed in 2025, so our results improved." The pass **rate** actually fell. By how many percentage points did it fall?
explanation: Pass rate 2024: $\frac{120}{160} \times 100 = 75\%$. Pass rate 2025: $\frac{135}{200} \times 100 = 67.5\%$. The pass rate fell by $75 - 67.5 = 7.5$ percentage points, even though the number passing rose because there were more candidates.
hints: Compare percentages, not numbers of passes, because the number of candidates changed.

stem:
The table shows the number of customers at a new clinic pharmacy each month.

| Month | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Customers | 310 | 325 | 342 | 360 | 381 | 395 |

Which statement describes the data best?

options.content: The number of customers increased every month.
options.rationale: Each value is larger than the one before.

options.content: The number of customers doubled over the six months.
options.rationale: $395$ is not double $310$.

options.content: The number of customers fell after month 4.
options.rationale: Months 5 and 6 are higher than month 4.

options.content: The number of customers stayed about the same.
options.rationale: It rose steadily by about 15 to 20 each month.

explanation: Each month's value is higher than the previous month's: $310 < 325 < 342 < 360 < 381 < 395$, so the number of customers increased every month. It did not double: $2 \times 310 = 620$.
